page.after:
What the differences mean

  • UGREEN HD151, 1 m: 1 m extension + 2 m attached cable = 3 m (9.8 ft) total at 8K60 or 4K240.
  • UGREEN HD151, 2 m: 2 m extension + 1 m attached cable = the same 3 m. The longer extension adds 0 m of total reach. It only shifts the 3 m from your cable to the extension.
  • A common mistake: a 2 m TV cable + the 2 m extension = 4 m, which is 1 m (3.3 ft) over UGREEN's limit, so 4K120 and 8K may drop out.
  • Cable Matters active extension: the cable is 6.6 ft long. The 16.4 ft figure is how far Cable Matters says it extends an 8K run, 16.4 − 6.6 = 9.8 ft more than the cable's own length, so buy it as a 6.6 ft cable.
  • OREI EX-230UHD: 230 ft at 1080p versus 131 ft at 4K60, so moving to 4K loses 230 − 131 = 99 ft of reach.
  • Long passive runs in testing: Linus Tech Tips' bench test of HDMI 2.1 cables failed 9 of 53 (9 ÷ 53 = 17%), and only 50% of its 15 ft cables passed.
Your setupWhat fits
Short gap behind a TV or console, 4K120 or 8K, existing cable 2 m or shorterUGREEN HD151, 1 m size
Port saver plugged straight into a PS5, Xbox or PCUGREEN HD151. The Cable Matters cable won't work reversed with its male plug in the source.
Extending at the TV end, 8K, with USB power nearbyCable Matters 48Gbps Active extension, female end toward the source
8K60 up to 33 ft between two cablesStarTech 33FT-8K-HDMI-BOOSTER
4K60 across a house, up to 131 ftOREI EX-230UHD over CAT6
4K120 over more than about 10 ft in totalSkip the extension. Use one certified Ultra High Speed HDMI cable at the full length.

The 3 m rule: how long an HDMI extension can be

A male-to-female extension doesn't regenerate the signal unless it's active. It adds its length to the cable already plugged into it, and at 48 Gbps the total run is what counts. UGREEN's HD151 listing says it directly: to reach 8K@60Hz or 4K@240Hz, the attached 30 AWG male cable must be no longer than 2 m (6.6 ft) with the 1 m extension, and no longer than 1 m (3.3 ft) with the 6.6 ft extension. Both combinations come to 3 m (9.8 ft). That's why the 1 m HD151 is the one to buy: it leaves the most room for the cable you already own. {buy:ugreen-hd151-8k-hdmi-2-1-extension-cable}

Linus Tech Tips' measurements back up the short-run advice. In its 53-cable HDMI 2.1 test, 6 ft Amazon Basics cables passed at 48 Gbps, while half of the 15 ft cables failed. Every Monoprice failure in that test was on a 10 ft or 15 ft cable, caused by signal integrity.

If you need more length at the TV end, Cable Matters' active extension uses electronics in the cable. That comes with two conditions from its own page. First, it is "NOT bi-directional": the female socket must connect to the source device and the male plug to the display. Second, its Micro-B USB power is "optional but recommended, especially for longer distances or 8K signals." HDMI.org explains why: an active cable can draw power over HDMI only when the source supports HDMI Cable Power; with other sources it needs a separate power connector. The page lists ARC (Audio Return Channel) but doesn't mention eARC, so soundbar and AVR owners who rely on eARC should test before they depend on it.

On certification, HDMI.org calls the Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable program mandatory, and certified cables carry a scannable label on the package. Neither extension's page shows that label. For 4K120 over long runs, one certified cable at the full length remains the safer route.

Not recommended

OREI EX-230UHD for 4K120 gaming. Its 230 ft rating applies to 1080p. OREI's support page limits 4K@60Hz to 131 ft (40 m) of CAT6 and says it does not support 4K@120Hz at any length, because it is an HDMI 2.0b, 18 Gbps device. It suits 4K60 video across a building, not a console feeding a 120 Hz TV.
